target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures define AMD's four reportable business segments (Data Center, Client, Gaming, Embedded) and list their primary product inclusions. D023 lists them for 2023, D017 for 2024, with similar descriptions.

Both disclosures state that in addition to the four reportable segments, AMD has an 'All Other' category which is not a reportable segment.

The 2023 disclosure (D023) explicitly lists four reportable segments: Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded. The 2024 disclosure (D019) states that beginning in fiscal year 2025, Client and Gaming will be combined into a single segment, resulting in three total segments. This represents a direct evolution of the segment reporting structure defined in the 2023 filing, specifically the consolidation of the Client and Gaming segments previously identified as separate entities. The topic correspondence is the definition and change of reportable segments within Item 1.

current_disclosures.summary: AMD's four reportable segments are Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded, each encompassing specific product lines for data centers, client devices, gaming hardware, and embedded solutions.
In addition to the four reportable segments, AMD maintains an All Other category which is not classified as a reportable segment.

Beginning with fiscal year 2025, AMD plans to combine the Client and Gaming segments into a single reportable segment to align with internal management structure, resulting in three total reportable segments.

comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA disclose specific, named reportable segments that define their primary business units. AMD identifies four reportable segments (Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded) in Item 1, noting an 'All Other' category that is not reportable. Similarly, NVIDIA describes its 'Compute & Networking' segment in Item 1, detailing its composition of Data Center platforms, automotive, and other embedded platforms. Both companies use Item 1 to establish the structural identity of their operational segments, with NVIDIA providing a detailed product mix within its named segment just as AMD lists its segment names.

The Compute & Networking segment is comprised of our Data Center accelerated computing platforms and end-to-end networking platforms including Quantum for InfiniBand and Spectrum for Ethernet; our NVIDIA DRIVE automated-driving platform and automotive development agreements; Jetson robotics and other embedded platforms; NVIDIA AI Enterprise and other software; and DGX Cloud software and services.
